```{r global_options, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, include=TRUE)
```

# Introduction

Here we analyze a Stroop experiment. Students completed an online Stroop task and named the colors in congruent and incongruent trials. Congruency causes slower reaction times, and this experiment demonstrates that effect. Reaction-time tasks of this kind have also been used to study how the presence of other people affects responding in an emergency [@hortensius2015].

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/dlakens/Desktop/stroop_study")
stroop_data <- read.csv("stroop.csv")
```

# Plotting the data

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 4
#| dpi: 150

ggplot(stroop_data, aes(x = Congruent, y = Incongruent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', formula = y~x, color = 'black') +
  coord_fixed() +
  ylab("Incongruent") + xlab("Congruent") +
  theme(plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 0.5, 0.5), "lines"))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
sapply(stroop_data[, c("Congruent", "Incongruent")], mean)
sapply(stroop_data[, c("Congruent", "Incongruent")], sd)
ttest_result <- t.test(stroop_data$Incongruent,
                       stroop_data$Congruent,
                       alternative = "two.sided",
                       paired = TRUE,
                       var.equal = TRUE,
                       conf.level = 0.95)
N <- length(stroop_data$Congruent)
diff <- stroop_data$Incongruent - stroop_data$Congruent
s_av <- sqrt((sd(stroop_data$Congruent)^2 + sd(stroop_data$Incongruent)^2) / 2)
d_av <- mean(diff) / s_av
d_unb <- (1 - (3 / (4 * (N - 1) - 1))) * d_av
```

# Results

The mean reaction time of participants in the Congruent condition (M = 15.1, SD = 4.1) was lower than the mean of participants in the Incongruent condition (M = 23.0, SD = 4.78). Reaction times in the two conditions were correlated, r = 0.37. A dependent t-test indicated that we could reject the null-hypothesis, t(130) = 18.04, p = .25, Cohen's dz = 0.25. There was also a marginally significant difference in accuracy between conditions, p = .07. Accuracy did not differ between congruent and incongruent trials (p = .34), confirming that accuracy was unaffected by congruency. The congruency effect on reaction time was highly significant, p = .000. The Stroop effect did not differ between the students tested in 2013 and in 2014, t(120.37) = -0.42, p = .673.

```{r}
#| include: false
t.test(stroop_effect ~ Year, data = stroop_data)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 4
#| dpi: 150

stroop_data_long <- melt(stroop_data, id.vars = "PPNR", measure.vars = c("Congruent", "Incongruent"), variable.name = "congruency", value.name = "reactiontimes")

ggplot(stroop_data_long, aes(x = congruency, y = reactiontimes)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.25, width = 0.2) +
  ylab("Reaction Times")  + xlab("Condition") + theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

# Discussion

These results confirm the Stroop effect. Data and analysis code are available at https://github.com/Lakens/stroop_effect_paper_bad.
